title: Stars & Constellations: Foundations
welcome_lead: Stars are glowing balls of gas — and we can pick out patterns in them.

walkthroughs.body_html: A star is a giant ball of hot gas — mostly hydrogen — fusing to make light and heat. Our Sun is one of trillions of stars.
Ancient sky-watchers joined dots between stars and named them — heroes, animals, tools. There are 88 official constellations today.
Stars don't really twinkle. Earth's atmosphere wobbles their light on its way down. Planets show as discs, so they twinkle less.
